Simulate Bolus Sensor Data

Source: R/bolus.R
simulate_bolus.Rd

Generates high-frequency synthetic bolus sensor data for each cow, mimicking the output of internal bolus sensor platforms (e.g. SmaXtec). Produces one row per cow per timestamp at a user-defined interval.

Usage

simulate_bolus(
  herd,
  days = 30,
  interval_mins = 10,
  start_date = Sys.Date(),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

herd

A tibble produced by simulate_herd().

days

Integer. Number of days of sensor data to generate per cow. Default is 30.

interval_mins

Integer. Sensor recording interval in minutes. Default is 10.

start_date

Date. Start date for the sensor records. Default is Sys.Date().

seed

Integer. Random seed for reproducibility. Default is NULL.

Value

A tibble with one row per cow per timestamp containing:

cow_id

Character. Links to simulate_herd() output.

date

Date. Calendar date of the reading.

timestamp

POSIXct. Date and time of the reading.

dim_at_reading

Integer. Days in milk on the date of the reading.

bolus_temp

Numeric. Internal body temperature (°C). Follows a circadian rhythm with spikes at mastitis and oestrus.

rumination_mins

Numeric. Rumination minutes in the interval. Peaks post-feeding; suppressed during mastitis and oestrus.

activity_index

Numeric. Activity level in the interval. Elevated during oestrus; suppressed during mastitis.

oestrus

Logical. TRUE if the cow is in oestrus on this day.

mastitis

Logical. TRUE if the cow has a mastitis event on this day.

Details

Biological patterns modelled:

Temperature follows a circadian rhythm with a daily minimum around 05:00 and maximum around 15:00 (amplitude ~0.5°C). Mastitis adds +0.5 to +2.5°C. Oestrus adds +0.3 to +0.8°C.

Rumination peaks twice daily (~08:00 and ~20:00, post-feeding). It is near zero during active oestrus and suppressed by 30–60% during mastitis.

Activity declines gradually with DIM. A strong spike (2–3x baseline) occurs over a 12–18 hour oestrus window. Mastitis suppresses activity by 20–40%.

Oestrus is assigned on a ~21-day cycle with a random phase per cow. It is detectable from the combined activity spike and temperature rise — mirroring real bolus platform alert logic.

Examples

herd   <- simulate_herd(10, seed = 42)
bolus  <- simulate_bolus(herd, days = 7, seed = 42)

# Custom interval
bolus15 <- simulate_bolus(herd, days = 7, interval_mins = 15, seed = 42)
